doc.title: Louie Bellson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Ellington years, Pearl Bailey and Jazz at the Philharmonic
title: Oscar Peterson's tempos and Duke's Big Four with Joe Pass
summary: Oscar Peterson played at fast tempos, and Bellson recalls Duke's near-last recording, Duke's Big Four with Joe Pass and Ray Brown.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Never heard it. So Benny Carter and I say, that’s Art Tatum. He and Oscar Peterson were two giants. Oscar overwhelmingly also, like Tatum. That tape we did with Oscar and John Heard is fabulous. We played Cute. You know what tempo they played it? It’s usually [Bellson sings the melody at a relaxed tempo]. Oscar played it [Bellson sings it at an extremely fast tempo].
How are you going to get your breaks in?

Then he turned around to me and laughed. Oh man. Then Sweet Georgia Brown is so fast, it’s unbelievable. Only he can play at those tempos. But I enjoyed working with Oscar, too. He was a giant musician. He could really play. Speaking of tapes, the next to last thing that Duke recorded was something we did out in California. I played drums. Joe Pass is on guitar and Ray Brown on bass and Duke. Just the four of us. You know about that one? He called it Duke’s Big Four.
Oh yeah. I remember seeing that. [?] for Pablo. Norman Granz [?].

Yeah. Norman Granz did it. Yeah. Norman did it. Pat Williard, I think, has a copy of that tape. That’s unbelievable. Duke had never heard Joe Pass play. He kept saying, “What’s that guy’s name?” Joe Pass. Joe Passalaqua is his real name. Joe Pass. He said, “Man, that guy could . . .” He was overcome with Joe Pass. Never heard anything like it. That’s [?]. It’s good. It’s a videotape. I asked you about that. She’s got the only copy of it. I may have a copy of it. I think I do have a copy of it. It’s been sitting around up there in the living room.
Was it commercially released? Are you talking about the CD? No . . .
CD. But there’s a video on it too. I think she’s got the video.
I’ve seen the CD, but I haven’t seen a video.
I’ve seen the video. It’s good.
In Hollywood. We recorded in Hollywood. We ran into [? ? ] with a long ponytail.
You’ll have to let me think about that. You guys are inspiring me to think about all these things.
